text_blocks.snippet: Several over-the-counter (OTC) medications contain anticholinergic ingredients. These include first-generation antihistamines like diphenhydramine (Benadryl) and doxylamine (Unisom), as well as medications for nausea and motion sickness like dimenhydrinate (Dramamine). These medications can be found in sleep aids, allergy medications, and anti-nausea products.
snippet_highlighted_words: first-generation antihistamines like diphenhydramine (Benadryl) and doxylamine (Unisom)

list.snippet: Antihistamines: First-generation antihistamines like diphenhydramine (found in Benadryl and various sleep aids like Tylenol PM and Advil PM), doxylamine (found in Unisom), and brompheniramine (found in Dimetapp) are known anticholinergics.
Anti-nausea medications: Dimenhydrinate, sold as Dramamine, is also an anticholinergic.
Sleep aids: Many OTC sleep aids, like some formulations of Benadryl, Tylenol PM, and Unisom, contain anticholinergic ingredients like diphenhydramine and doxylamine.

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to note that some prescription medications, like certain antidepressants and antipsychotics, also have anticholinergic effects. When considering OTC medications, it's always a good idea to check the labels for active ingredients and consult with a pharmacist or doctor if you have any concerns, especially if you are taking other medications or have any underlying health conditions.

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, several anticholinergic drugs are available over-the-counter (OTC). These medications are often used to treat allergies, insomnia, motion sickness, and certain digestive issues. Examples include diphenhydramine (Benadryl), dimenhydrinate (Dramamine), and doxylamine (Unisom).

list.snippet: Diphenhydramine (Benadryl, Tylenol PM, Advil PM, Unisom SleepGels): Used for allergies, cold symptoms, and sleep.
Brompheniramine (Dimetapp): Used for allergy and cold symptoms.

list.title: Side Effects:
list.snippet: Anticholinergic medications can cause side effects such as drowsiness, dry mouth, constipation, and blurred vision.

list.title: Elderly Patients:
list.snippet: Older adults may be more susceptible to anticholinergic side effects, including confusion and cognitive impairment.

list.title: Interactions:
list.snippet: Anticholinergic drugs can interact with other medications. It's crucial to discuss any OTC medications with a pharmacist or doctor, especially if you have other health conditions or are taking other medications.

list.title: Alternatives:
list.snippet: For allergies, newer antihistamines like loratadine (Claritin) and cetirizine (Zyrtec) are often preferred as they have fewer anticholinergic effects. For sleep, consider non-anticholinergic options like melatonin.
